intended_object: The reduction (residue) ring homomorphism from the ring of (a)-adically restricted power series R⟨X_σ⟩ over a local ring R, with a ∈ 𝔪, to polynomials over the residue field k[X_σ]. It sends Σ c_d X^d to Σ (c_d mod 𝔪) X^d. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body applies the library's general `reductionAtLargerIdeal I J` with I = (a) and J = 𝔪. The inclusion (a) ≤ 𝔪 comes from the hypothesis a ∈ 𝔪. Its coefficient lemma `coeff_reductionAtLargerIdeal` shows that the d-th coefficient of the image is `coeff d f mod 𝔪`, so the map is exactly reduction of coefficients modulo the maximal ideal.

The image really is a polynomial. An (a)-adically restricted series has only finitely many coefficients outside (a) ⊆ 𝔪, so only finitely many coefficients survive modulo 𝔪. This is the standard reduction map R⟨X⟩ → k[X] used in the theory of restricted power series. In the same file, the library checks that it agrees with its earlier `restrictedResidue` function over valuation domains.

The restriction to a principal ideal and a local ring is the intended setting of this named residue map. The general version (any I ≤ J) already exists in the library as `reductionAtLargerIdeal`, and this definition is just that version specialised to the residue field. Mathlib has no restricted-power-series residue map. The definition is therefore faithful.
